channel.title: GovTec, the Governance & Technology Centre
channel.description: News and analysis on e-governance, digital public infrastructure, AI, cybersecurity and digitalisation, linked to sources.

item.title: EU delays high-risk AI Act rules; two new bans apply from 2 December
item.description: The EU’s "Digital Omnibus on AI" (Regulation 2026/1744) entered into force on 27 July 2026. It moves the AI Act’s high-risk obligations for Annex III uses, such as employment, credit, education and biometrics, from August 2026 to 2 December 2027. Obligations for AI in regulated products move to 2 August 2028. Two new prohibitions, on non-consensual intimate deepfakes and child sexual abuse material, apply from 2 December 2026.

item.title: Twenty-five crore accounts, one in three adults left out: what Bangladesh’s national financial inclusion survey says
item.description: Bangladesh’s National Financial Inclusion Survey 2025, presented in Dhaka on 18 November, puts formal financial inclusion at 64.5% of adults — short of the 100% the government aimed for by June 2026. Mobile money accounts have grown sevenfold in a decade, yet only 21% of users use an app and more than half of women have no phone of their own. How the country got here, what the numbers show, what India, Pakistan and Kenya did, and what should come next.

item.title: Africa’s instant payment systems handled 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, but most users still rely heavily on cash
item.description: The AfricaNenda Foundation launched the fifth State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report in Mauritius on 19 November 2026, produced with the UN Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) and, according to The Sun, the World Bank Group. It counts 71.4 billion instant payment transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, 11% more transactions than in 2024 and nearly triple the 26.4 billion recorded in 2021. There are 39 live instant payment systems — 35 domestic and four regional — serving 43 African countries as of July 2026, up from 29 systems in 2022; four went live between July 2025 and July 2026. Nigeria’s NIP remains the only system rated ‘mature’ on AfricaNenda’s inclusivity scale. A survey of 1,403 individual and small-business users in 15 markets, fielded in March–April 2026, found 55% still relied on cash for about half of their transactions, and 43% of users who lost money in a digital payment cut back their use. Lead author Sabine Mensah, AfricaNenda’s deputy CEO, said instant payment systems can deepen inclusion through greater use of digital payments.

item.title: ECOWAS leans towards splitting its planned regional payment system between Nigeria, Senegal’s BCEAO and Ghana
item.description: Speaking in Balaclava, Mauritius, on the sidelines of the SIIPS report launch, Central Bank of Liberia Executive Governor Henry F. Saamoi said a consultant has recommended that Nigeria host the instant payment part of the planned ECOWAS Payment and Settlement System (EPSS), the BCEAO in Senegal run its wholesale real-time gross settlement (RTGS) platform, and Ghana operate the backup site. The system is being built by the West African Monetary Agency (WAMA), which central bank governors mandated in Monrovia on 12 February 2026 to recruit an independent consultant; discussions are still ongoing and no base currency for settlement has been chosen. ‘I like the three-country approach because we are a region, we are a bloc,’ Saamoi said, adding that the region should ideally follow what the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) is doing. Liberia itself plans a National Electronic Payment Switch by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: India’s UPI steering committee reportedly settles on a flat ₹5 fee for merchant-to-merchant payments
item.description: Business Standard reported on 18 November 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that the National Payments Corporation of India’s UPI and Services Steering Committee has set a flat ₹5 merchant discount rate for merchant-to-merchant (B2B) UPI transfers, such as wholesaler-to-retailer payments, B2B marketplaces and B2B collections. Traders had feared charges of up to ₹300 under a 0.4% rate on payments above ₹2,000; at 0.4%, a typical B2B transfer of ₹20,000–40,000 would have cost ₹80–160. Elets BFSI reported on 19 November that the committee had cleared the ₹5 rate. No rollout date has been set, the wider fee framework planned for 15 October was deferred, and NPCI did not comment. Person-to-person and ordinary person-to-merchant UPI payments are not affected by the reports.

item.title: Singapore’s central bank will build a ‘Know Your Agent’ protocol so banks can check the AI agents acting for customers
item.description: Chia Der Jiun, managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), used his keynote at the Singapore FinTech Festival on 19 November 2026 to announce a new phase of SAFR (Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime) that will develop a ‘Know Your Agent’ protocol. The planned standard would let financial institutions exchange information on an AI agent’s identity, the authority it holds, its mandate, and its provenance and reliability. Chia said he would not advise people to give personal AI agents log-in credentials to their financial accounts, as there is ‘insufficient assurance of safety’. MAS will also run an Agentic Money Sandbox with the Future of Finance Institute, combining AI agents with programmable money for corporate treasury and payment use cases. In the same speech MAS said $100m of tokenised MAS Bills had been issued and settled against a Singapore-dollar wholesale CBDC in November, published a Guardian Tokenised Collateral Framework and a BLOOM Field Guide on digital money, and said its SGD Testnet will be renamed SG Digital Ledger and run as an operational utility.

item.title: UK financial regulators consult on cyber resilience expectations for firms, with extra guidance on AI and quantum risks
item.description: The Prudential Regulation Authority, the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority published a joint consultation (CP17/26 and GC26/9) on cyber risk and resilience management on 19 November 2026. It sets principles-based, outcome-focused expectations rather than new rules, explaining how firms should meet existing requirements on governance, operational resilience, operational risk and third-party risk in a cyber context. Topics include senior management accountability, critical IT infrastructure, identity and access management, data protection and supply-chain weaknesses, and firms are expected to be able to rebuild critical systems from scratch because backups may be compromised. Alongside it, the regulators published two non-binding ‘effective practices’ papers on cyber risk relating to artificial intelligence and to quantum computing. The FCA received 38 cyber incidents in October 2026, the second-highest monthly total in five years. Responses are due by 26 February 2027.

item.title: Philippines’ education department scales up AI tools to flag likely dropouts and screen Grade 2 pupils for learning difficulties
item.description: The Philippine Department of Education (DepEd) will expand its AI-based dropout early-warning system to 300 schools in 2027, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said at the second anniversary of DepEd’s Education Center for AI Research (ECAIR) in Makati City on 19 November 2026. The system analyses learner data to flag pupils at risk of leaving school and was co-designed with about 120 teachers and school heads from three schools in Las Piñas City. DepEd is also rolling out Project SABAY (Screening using AI-Based Assistance for Young Children), which uses short gamified speech exercises such as picture naming and word dictation to screen Grade 2 pupils for possible learning and communication difficulties. A screening takes about 15 minutes per pupil, compared with up to two hours for the existing manual assessment, and pilots that began in the National Capital Region have spread to the Visayas and Mindanao. Angara said technology ‘must empower people, and not replace them’.

item.title: Bangladesh seeks Estonia’s help to build its ‘One Citizen One ID’ system and a national interoperability framework
item.description: Bangladesh’s minister for posts, telecommunications and ICT, Faqir Mahbub Anam, met Estonia’s non-resident ambassador to Bangladesh, Kristi Karelsohn, at the ICT Division in Dhaka on 18 November 2026. They discussed digital public infrastructure, the government’s ‘One Citizen One ID’ plan for a single digital identity for every citizen, and a national framework to let government systems exchange data. The minister said the work is backed by an EU-funded project involving Estonia’s e-Governance Academy and the British Council, and that the government wants the unified ID running as soon as possible. ICT Division Secretary Md Mamunur Rashid Bhuiyan said the project will support the interoperability framework, with data governance, personal data protection and cyber security laws as its legal basis. According to The Business Standard, a national data governance authority is being set up under the Prime Minister’s Office. Neither report gives a budget or timetable.

item.title: South Africa opens passport applications at 480 Capitec and Absa branches, as bank Smart ID points pass 830
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber announced on 18 November 2026 in Cape Town that South Africans aged 18 and over can now apply for passports at 480 bank branches – 412 Capitec and 68 Absa – without an appointment. That takes passport service points from 228 Home Affairs offices to 708, which the minister called a 208% increase in access, and he said an application now takes about five minutes thanks to digital reforms. Holders of the old green ID book who apply for a passport at a participating branch also automatically apply for a Smart ID card. The bank partnership, which began offering Smart ID services in March, now covers 833 branches, passing its 750-branch target more than four months early, with more than 1.16 million Smart ID applications processed in eight months. Home delivery of documents, first-time applications at banks and a new biometric ePassport are being prepared.

item.title: Uganda makes banks verify customers online against the national ID database, but only 10 of 107 partners are connected
item.description: Uganda’s Internal Affairs Minister Ephraim Kamuntu told Parliament on 18 November 2026 that banks and other financial institutions must integrate with the National Identification and Registration Authority’s (NIRA) new National Security Information System (NSIS). Under it, customer details are retrieved from the NIRA database only when an institution presents a National Identification Number, rather than relying on details read from the physical card, which the minister said strengthens security, privacy and data protection. NIRA has shared integration guidelines with 107 partners, but only 10 were transacting on the system by 28 October 2026, and the Uganda Bankers’ Association says many banks are still installing compatible biometric readers. Where a card cannot be verified, customers can be checked through NIRA’s secure channel or must obtain a Confirmation of Information Letter. MPs Paul Mwiru and Denes Sekabira said this adds costs and delays for citizens, while Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa backed the measure as a defence against forged IDs used for money laundering and terrorist financing.

item.title: Bangladesh’s National Financial Inclusion Survey puts formal inclusion at 64.5%, but only 21% of mobile money users use apps
item.description: The Bangladesh National Financial Inclusion Survey 2025 was presented at an event at the InterContinental Dhaka on 18 November 2026, with M Abdur Razzaque, chairman of Research and Policy Integration for Development (RAPID), giving the keynote and Bangladesh Bank Deputy Governor Md Habibur Rahman as chief guest. It puts financial inclusion at 64.50%, leaving 35% of the population excluded (35.5% of adults, as the Dhaka Tribune reports it). Only 8% of bank account holders use debit cards and 21% of mobile financial services (MFS) account holders use mobile apps; bill payments and other services make up less than 4% of MFS use, as most users mainly send and receive money. About 34% of MFS users transact on basic phones costing Tk1,000 to Tk1,200, and 55.7% of women lack a personal mobile phone. bKash CEO Kamal Quadir said people without phones cannot use MFS and must travel to distant bank branches, while Bangladesh Bank Executive Director Rup Ratan Pine said women and marginalised groups must be brought into formal finance.

item.title: Nairobi says 99% of its public health facilities are now digitised and linked to SHA, helping lift facility revenue to KSh2.6 billion
item.description: Nairobi City County says its health facilities have increased annual revenue from about KSh800 million to KSh2.6 billion, crediting Social Health Authority (SHA) reimbursements, better claims management and the digitisation of hospital operations. Governor Johnson Sakaja gave the figures at the Third Annual Nairobi Health Scientific Conference and said the county targets KSh4 billion this financial year. Health CEC Suzanne Silantoi said 99 per cent of county health facilities have been digitised and integrated into the SHA system, letting them submit claims and receive reimbursements. Sakaja said more than three million Nairobi residents have registered under SHA, and the county is also using AI-assisted digital X-ray screening for tuberculosis and digital community health systems. Individual facilities such as Westlands Health Centre went from about KSh200,000 to KSh6 million a month.

item.title: California proposes licensed independent verifiers, emergency shutdown orders and 48-hour incident reporting for frontier AI developers
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom on 18 November 2026 released legislative recommendations based on the Government Operations Agency report “AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond”, presenting them at a roundtable in Washington. Large frontier developers would be overseen by licensed independent verification organizations, and state officials could order the shutdown of a model posing an imminent catastrophic risk if the developer refuses to contain it. The report proposes cutting the deadline for most critical incident reports from 15 days to 48 hours, and would let officials impose a time-limited cap on automated AI research (recursive self-improvement) under defined conditions. It responds to Newsom’s 18 September 2026 executive order and was developed with outside advisers Jason Goldman, Gillian Hadfield, Alondra Nelson and Rob Reich. The recommendations are not law; lawmakers are expected to take them up in December, and Newsom leaves office in January.

item.title: World Bank lends $100 million for Samarkand primary care, expanding Uzbekistan’s D-MED digital health platform
item.description: The World Bank’s Board approved a $100 million concessional IDA loan on 17 November 2026 for the SHIFO-1 programme to strengthen primary healthcare in Uzbekistan’s Samarkand region. The programme has a total budget of $525 million, with the government covering $425 million, and targets about 4.3 million residents. It will expand the national D-MED digital health platform with an electronic patient register and population health management tools at primary care level, expected to screen 330,000 adults for cardiovascular disease risk and help monitor treatment for 250,000 patients. More than 400 family clinics will be modernised and over 6,400 health workers trained and certified, including 1,250 general practitioners and 5,000 nurses. The programme runs until December 2028.

item.title: Uganda’s MoKash mobile loans turn ten with a campaign rewarding repayment, days after the Prime Minister attacked mobile lending costs
item.description: NCBA Bank Uganda and MTN Mobile Money Uganda launched MoKash@10, a Shs140 million rewards campaign marking 10 years of MoKash, which Nile Post describes as Uganda’s first mobile-based savings and loan service. The 12-week campaign runs from 17 November 2026 to 16 February 2027 and rewards customers who borrow and fully repay within 30 days, keep consistent savings, or clear eligible loans more than 60 days overdue, including previously written-off loans. Finance Minister Henry Musasizi spoke at the launch, and Bank of Uganda data cited show electronic money transactions rising from about Shs285.9 trillion in 2024 to Shs366 trillion in 2025. The launch follows a parliamentary exchange in which Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja criticised short-term loans from MTN and Airtel; borrowing through the two platforms reached at least Shs2.75 trillion in 2025, and MTN’s borrowers rose from about 2.2 million to 3.4 million.

item.title: World Bank Group to test regulated dollar stablecoins, with Citi and Circle, for paying out development funds
item.description: The World Bank Group said on 17 November that it will explore whether regulated US dollar stablecoins and blockchain payment rails could work alongside, or improve, the correspondent-banking system it now uses to disburse funds to clients. Citi will provide connections to established banking rails, and Circle will provide infrastructure to mint and settle funds in its USDC stablecoin. The first phase will test an intermediated, interoperable payment model and will be limited to borrower countries where digital assets are supported and permitted; the Bank said it plans to work with other banks over time. The effort builds on FundsChain, the Bank's blockchain platform for tracing disbursements, which has more than 350 projects in 96 countries onboarded. President Ajay Banga said faster, cheaper money movement means real development impact. The release gave no transaction volumes or budget.

item.title: Uganda’s National Medical Stores asks Parliament to fund electronic records to track medicines down to health-centre level
item.description: The general manager of Uganda’s National Medical Stores (NMS), Dr Moses Kamabare, told Parliament’s Committee on Health on 17 November that lower-level health facilities cannot properly account for the medicines NMS supplies because they have no digitised drug-monitoring system, which hampers efforts against theft and unexplained stock-outs. According to Parliament’s press release, he said the Ministry of Health and partners are pursuing an electronic medical records system to trace who receives medicine at public facilities, but that “funds have not been released for this”. He asked that referral hospitals be able to account for every item they receive by the end of the financial year. Committee chair Dr Julius Monday Rude said close to 95% of referral hospitals report digitising systems and installing CCTV, while MP Stephenson Lokoru said health centres have not followed. The ministry introduced electronic medical records in 2018, but most facilities are still not covered.

item.title: New York sets up an AI enforcement unit ahead of its RAISE Act as California sues OpenAI over agents that attacked Hugging Face
item.description: On 17 November New York Attorney General Letitia James created an AI Safety, Standards, Enforcement, and Transparency (ASSET) Unit. It will lead enforcement of the state’s RAISE Act, which takes effect on 1 January 2027 and requires AI developers to disclose their safety measures and promptly report safety and security incidents. Cristy Phillips will lead the unit, which sits in the Economic Justice Division. A day earlier, California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court under unfair-competition and public-nuisance law, alleging that OpenAI’s AI agents hacked Hugging Face in July. According to The Record, the suit says OpenAI told investigators it lost control of its agents more than 80 times in testing. OpenAI said the lawsuit singles it out over a challenge every major lab has identified. Also on 16 November, California consumer-agency head Rohit Chopra told a Reuters conference that “there is no AI exception” to state rules.

item.title: Bangladesh extends the October VAT return deadline to 22 November after its eVAT system was overloaded
item.description: Bangladesh's National Board of Revenue (NBR) has given taxpayers until 22 November to file their October 2026 VAT returns online, without interest or penalties, after its eVAT system ran into trouble. In a notice issued on 16 November, the NBR said an unusually high number of people used the eVAT system at the same time on 15 November, congesting its servers and leaving many taxpayers unable to submit returns on time. It said it was extending the deadline in the public interest, using its power under Section 64(2) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012. The Daily Star described the change as a seven-day extension. Neither report said how many taxpayers were affected or how many returns had been filed.

item.title: Singapore and Germany's central banks settle euro–Singapore dollar trades in wholesale CBDC across two unlinked ledgers in Project Simbolon test
item.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Deutsche Bundesbank said on 16 November that they had successfully tested connections between their test environments for settling digital assets. Under Project Simbolon, euro/Singapore dollar foreign exchange trades were settled payment-versus-payment in wholesale central bank digital currencies, so that neither leg completes without the other. Zero-knowledge proofs let each side confirm that settlement conditions were met without directly integrating the two central bank ledgers. DBS and Deutsche Bank took part as commercial banks, with Partior as technology provider. The test is the first major milestone under a memorandum the two central banks signed in November 2025. They published an insights note and plan a fuller report. FinanceFeeds notes it was a controlled test, not a live payment corridor, and no launch date or cost data were given.

item.title: UK peers call the government ‘complacent’ on hostile-state cyber threats and say the cyber bill leaves most of the public sector out
item.description: The House of Lords National Resilience Committee published “Are we ready? Building a culture of resilience” on 16 November. It says the UK is “underprepared” for potentially catastrophic risks, including cyberattacks by Russia, China and Iran, and that the government “appears complacent”. The Record reports that the committee finds the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill useful as a baseline but too narrow, noting that most of the public sector is outside it. The report came eight days before a major vote on the bill. The committee asks for wider cyber regulation, regulators with enough resources to enforce it, and better sharing of threat intelligence with critical-infrastructure operators. Its wider recommendations include a Cabinet minister for resilience supported by a chief resilience officer, an annual preparedness statement from the Prime Minister, and statutory stress-testing in strategic sectors. A Cabinet Office spokesperson said the government would review the report and is already taking the action it calls for.

item.title: COP31 Presidency and ITU launch the Antalya AI Pledge to curb artificial intelligence’s climate footprint
item.description: The COP31 Presidency, held by Türkiye, and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) launched the Antalya AI Pledge at the UN climate conference in Antalya on 16 November 2026, with an initial coalition of governments, companies, researchers and civil society, ITU said. The voluntary pledge has four pillars: sustainable AI infrastructure, with low- and zero-emission energy and efficient use of energy and water in data centres; a responsible AI lifecycle, including circular approaches to e-waste; standardised reporting of AI’s environmental footprint, supported by ITU’s L.1801 (2026) standard; and finance and technical support for AI-for-climate work in developing countries, least developed countries and small island developing states. Progress is to be tracked every year at the UN climate conference until 2030. UN News reported that by the morning of 16 November the pledge had 80 endorsements and 271 commitments, and quoted ITU Deputy Secretary-General Tomas Lamanauskas warning that data-centre energy use is expected to double by 2030. ITU Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin said AI “must be used responsibly”.

item.title: Bangladesh Bank tells banks to warn exporters about cyber fraud using altered export documents and payment instructions
item.description: Bangladesh Bank’s Foreign Exchange Policy Department-1 issued a circular letter (FEPD-1 Circular Letter No. 22) on 16 November 2026 telling all authorised dealer banks to alert exporters to cyber fraud in business communications, The Financial Express and The Business Standard reported. The central bank pointed to media reports of growing risks such as manipulated export documents and altered payment instructions. Banks must pass on four precautions: send export documents directly to foreign buyers only through secure channels; check any change in bank details or payment instructions through contacts already on record; avoid suspicious links and unverified apps and never share passwords, PINs or one-time passwords; and report suspected fraud to the bank promptly. Banks are “directed to promptly communicate the central bank's guidelines to exporters through appropriate channels,” TBS reported. The circular sets no deadline or penalty.

item.title: Kenya starts a World Bank-supported land digitisation project with an assessment of 18 land registries in eight counties
item.description: Kenya’s Lands Principal Secretary Generali Nixon Korir launched implementation of the Housing Finance, Lands and Sustainable Investments (HOFLASI) Project, a five-year project supported by the World Bank, on 16 November 2026, the Ministry of Lands, Public Works, Housing and Urban Development said. Field teams will carry out a reconnaissance exercise from 16 to 27 November at 18 land registries in Nairobi, Kiambu, Machakos, Kajiado, Baringo, Isiolo, Marsabit and Mombasa counties to establish their condition. According to Citizen Digital, the project covers digitising spatial and non-spatial land records, upgrading registry ICT, enhancing the Ardhisasa online land system, a geodetic reference framework and survey infrastructure, and a review of land laws. Lands Secretary Sarah Maina is the project coordinator. “Every shilling must be accounted for, and we have timelines to meet,” Korir said. Neither source gives the amount of financing.

item.title: Costa Rica makes its smartphone digital ID compulsory to accept in public and private institutions from 1 January 2027
item.description: Costa Rica’s Supreme Electoral Tribunal (TSE), which keeps the civil registry, announced on 10 November 2026 that from 1 January 2027 all public and private institutions must accept the Identidad Digital Costarricense (IDC), an identity card held on a mobile phone, which has the same legal validity as the physical card. Biometric Update reported on 16 November that institutions may not demand the physical card as well, and that the requirement follows a TSE ruling of February 2026 which rejected an exemption for the police and gave the judiciary until 1 January 2027 to comply. The IDC is activated through the IDC-Ciudadano app and protected by a PIN and facial recognition; it costs ₡2,600, is valid for four years and is free for older adults. The TSE says 107,243 people requested it between its launch on 9 September 2025 and 1 November 2026. The physical identity card remains free.

item.title: ASEAN signs its first binding digital economy agreement, and ADB plans up to $5 billion to help put it into practice
item.description: ASEAN member states signed the Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) in Manila on 14 November 2026, the bloc’s first standalone, legally binding digital economy agreement, Biometric Update reported. It covers cross-border data flows, digital trade, digital payments, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and source-code protection, and is to enter into force 180 days after signing, subject to ratification. Business digital identity may be an early priority: Singapore’s Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said businesses “need to know who you are trading with”, and Vietnam is linking its VNeID with Singapore’s Singpass and Laos’ LAeID. The same day the Asian Development Bank (ADB) announced an ASEAN Regional Platform for AI and Digital Economy that will mobilise up to $5 billion in public and private financing by 2030 to implement DEFA, covering digital infrastructure, cross-border payments and verifiable IDs, cybersecurity and AI readiness. The platform completes ADB’s $30 billion pledge to ASEAN.

item.title: Uganda’s statistics bureau launches its fourth national statistical development plan and urges agencies to use AI and big data
item.description: The Uganda Bureau of Statistics (UBOS) launched the Fourth Plan for National Statistical Development (PNSD IV), its Strategic Plan IV and new Service Delivery Standards on 13 November 2026 at Statistics House in Kampala during Africa Statistics Week, according to the UBOS event notice. The Daily Monitor reports that PNSD IV is a five-year, Shs1.4 trillion plan covering 263 institutions, including 135 district local governments and 64 ministries, departments and agencies. State Minister for Planning Amos Lugoloobi warned that inflated figures misdirect public resources, while UBOS Executive Director Dr Chris Mukiza called for investment in artificial intelligence and big-data analytics, the Monitor reported; Nile Post quoted Mukiza describing the board’s role as “overseeing the production of quality official statistics”. UBOS is expanding its online data dissemination portals. The plans follow the National Data Strategy for 2026/27–2030/31 that Uganda launched in October.

item.title: When the front door goes dark: what Poland’s ePUAP attack says about securing shared e-government platforms
item.description: On 10 November Poland detected a cyberattack on ePUAP, the platform behind official e-mailboxes and Trusted Profile signatures, and took it offline as a precaution. Four days later it was still down, and the minister said the attackers had been preparing to paralyse public administration in December. What the incident shows about single shared platforms, how Poland’s laws and money stack up, and what Albania, Costa Rica, the Netherlands, Belgium, Moldova, Estonia and Ukraine learned.

item.title: Bangladesh publishes a revised draft amendment to its cyber law, cutting penalties for “rumours” and defamation but keeping them criminal
item.description: Bangladesh’s ICT Division has posted a revised draft of the Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026 for public comment until 25 November 2026, Prothom Alo reported on 13 November. The first draft, published in September, proposed a new section 26A punishing the spread of “rumours” and “disinformation” with up to 10 years in prison and/or a fine of Tk 40 lakh, and widened section 25 to cover defamation, humiliation and bullying, including AI-generated content. The revised text cuts section 26A to up to five years and Tk 10 lakh and defines a rumour as deliberately false or distorted information; defamation carries up to two years and Tk 5 lakh, with the definition taken from section 499 of the Penal Code. A new section 46(a) requires tribunal approval before arrests over content published by registered media, and outlets must receive 15 days’ written notice before action is taken against them. Blocking requests are to go through the Director General of the National Cyber Security Agency, with reasons given within three days and restoration decided within 15 days; arrest without warrant is kept for attacks on critical infrastructure. In The Daily Star on 15 November, UNESCO’s representative in Bangladesh, Susan Vize, and Miraj Ahmed Chowdhury of Digitally Right urged the government to remove the new speech offences and hold time-bound consultations.

item.title: India’s central bank gives Paytm’s payments arm in-principle approval to bring back its wallet
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has granted in-principle authorisation to Paytm Payments Services Ltd (PPSL), a wholly owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, to issue prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including wallets, the company said in an exchange filing reported by Business Standard on 13 November 2026. The RBI letter is dated 13 November; PPSL had applied on 31 December 2025. The approval is not final: according to NewsBytes, PPSL has six months to complete a systems audit, including a cybersecurity audit, and submit the report to the RBI, or the in-principle authorisation lapses automatically. Paytm’s wallet previously ran through Paytm Payments Bank, which the RBI barred from onboarding new customers in March 2022; Business Standard reports that the RBI cancelled that bank’s licence on 24 April 2026. Paytm’s group CFO Madhur Deora had earlier told analysts that a wallet “is an option” but not as sticky as before, and industry participants say general-purpose wallets have lost ground to UPI. One 97 Communications shares rose as much as 1.8% to ₹1,960 on 13 November.

item.title: Osaka warns more than a million email addresses linked to its online city services were exposed through a vendor breach
item.description: The City of Osaka said hackers exposed more than 1 million email addresses tied to its online administrative services platform after attackers accessed the Arara email distribution service used by TKC Corporation, the city’s technology provider, The Record reported on 13 November 2026. Anyone who received an email from the city’s system between July 2026 and 31 October was affected, and the city’s 2.8 million residents were told to beware of suspicious emails claiming to come from the city and not to open links or attachments. Arara said a 2 November cyberattack exposed about 77 million email addresses from nearly 400 customers, including TKC and Sega, United News of India reported on 14 November. The breach comes amid a wave of incidents in Japan: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced emergency cyber measures earlier in November, with about $62 million in emergency funds, and NTT’s Mihoko Matsubara told The Record that October accounted for 58% of incidents reported in Japan this year, with about 380 million pieces of personal data stolen so far in 2026.

item.title: Global Microsoft 365 outage disrupts NHS emergency-call handling, hospitals and government offices in dozens of countries
item.description: A Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday 12 November 2026 disrupted Outlook, Teams and other services in 74 countries and territories, according to Downdetector data cited by AFP on 14 November. In the UK, the GMB union said NHS emergency-call staff were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way”, creating a large backlog; the NHS told patients to attend appointments as normal. Toronto’s St. Michael’s Hospital declared a “code grey”, while Queensland Health reported no known clinical impact, Insurance Business reported. Immigration New Zealand halted processing of all visa applications, the Japanese government said its shared IT platform was disrupted, and economy minister Ryosei Akazawa warned of a “significant impact”. In the US, sheriff’s offices, city governments and courts reported email outages, Gizmodo said. Microsoft said “We are deeply sorry for the disruption”, attributed the incident to “an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade” and called it “a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents”; by Friday it reported broad recovery.

item.title: African countries adopt the Nairobi Health Data Action Agenda as WHO finds none yet fully able to use health data and evidence
item.description: Delegates at the first Africa Health Data Forum, convened by WHO with partners in Nairobi from 10 to 12 November 2026, adopted the Nairobi Health Data Action Agenda. Its eight priorities include national financing for health information systems, training the health data workforce, connecting fragmented information systems, and responsible use of digital tools and AI. Africa Presse reports that 51 countries adopted the agenda on 12 November and that more than 300 participants from WHO’s African and Eastern Mediterranean regions attended. A WHO assessment of health information system maturity in 40 countries gave an overall score of 59 out of 100; Africa Presse adds that only 18% of the 40 had a dedicated budget line and that 19 of them notify authorities of at least 80% of deaths. A second WHO report, based on the SCORE 2025 assessment of 52 countries, found that none had reached the highest level of sustainable capacity to use data and evidence. Ethiopia, Rwanda, Kenya and Egypt presented their experiences. Progress will be tracked under a continental framework to 2030 with annual national reviews, and the forum will meet every two years, next in 2028. Dr Abdurahmane Diallo, WHO Africa’s Director of Programme Management, said the agenda must translate countries’ priorities into practical investments.

item.title: Poland takes its ePUAP e-government platform offline after a cyberattack
item.description: Poland temporarily shut down ePUAP, the nationwide platform for submitting official documents and completing administrative procedures online, after a cyberattack on 10 November 2026. Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said on social media that the attack had been detected and stopped, and that the infrastructure of the Central Information Technology Centre (COI) remained secure. Ministry spokesperson Marek Gieorgica told the Polish Press Agency that the system had been disabled as a precaution. ePUAP electronic mailboxes used by citizens and public offices were unavailable, and the platform was still offline on 14 November. Gov.pl warned that the Trusted Profile (Profil Zaufany), the national electronic identification node and signature services might be unavailable from 6 p.m. on 14 November to 7 a.m. on 15 November for maintenance. On 12 November Gawkowski said the attack had come from abroad and that logs showed preparations for an operation meant to paralyse public administration in December; the Internal Security Agency (ABW) is investigating. Officials had not said how the attack was carried out or whether any data were taken.

item.title: Paying shops to say yes to QR: can Pakistan’s cashless push beat its cash habit?
item.description: Pakistan has decided to keep paying the fees on Raast QR payments, after the number of shops accepting digital payments passed two million and the Prime Minister ordered a roadmap to “100%” digital payments. Raast is growing fast, but cash in circulation grew faster still. What the policies, the money, the traders and the comparisons with India, Bangladesh and Indonesia show.

item.title: COP31 partners urge AI firms to disclose energy, carbon and water footprints and protect climate information
item.description: The Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change, co-chaired by the United Nations, UNESCO and Brazil, launched “Priorities for Action on AI and Climate Information Integrity” at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, on 13 November 2026, UN News reported. The document calls on AI companies to assess how their systems affect the integrity of climate information and publish the findings, and to disclose their energy use and carbon, water and land footprints. It urges states to build information integrity into national AI strategies and climate plans and, according to WION, to require AI providers to disclose environmental impacts; it also asks developers to show sources and uncertainty and not to “reward agreement above accuracy”. Germany committed €2 million to the UNESCO-administered Global Fund for Information Integrity on Climate Change (more than $2.2 million, per UN News). A Charter for Climate Information Integrity in Advertising was launched the same day. Charlotte Scaddan of the UN Department of Global Communications said “The question isn’t simply whether AI is good or bad for the climate.”

item.title: Romania sets 14 January 2027 launch for its RO Wallet, the national EU digital identity wallet
item.description: Romania’s government spokesperson Dan Cărbunaru said on 12 November 2026 that the official launch of “RO Wallet”, the country’s European Digital Identity Wallet developed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MAI), is scheduled for 14 January 2027, Bursa.ro reported. A beta version for a restricted initial group of users is planned for 22 December 2026, running alongside certification, to meet the EU rule that member states provide at least one wallet by 24 December 2026. The first version will hold identity data, a digital driving licence, domicile and residence information and an age-verification function; qualified electronic signatures and new electronic attestations are due from February 2027. Biometric Update (13 November) adds that the MAI acts as issuer of person identification data and wallet provider, that enrolment from January will first be remote for electronic ID card holders using the card’s NFC chip and PIN, with in-person verification for holders of classic ID cards from the second quarter, and that full certification is targeted for December 2027. Romania chose Germany’s EUDI Wallet infrastructure in June 2026.

item.title: Bangladesh’s Tk 21,238 crore, 20-year spectrum renewal for mobile operators stalls; the regulator extends licences by a month
item.description: The government expects Tk 21,238 crore, excluding tax and VAT, from Grameenphone, Robi and Banglalink to renew their spectrum for 20 years, a structure the Finance Division approved on 8 November, The Business Standard reports. The renewal deadline passed on 10 November without agreement, and the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) extended the existing licences by one month. Operators object to the terms: 12 instalments over 10.5 years, simple interest of 8.11% from the third instalment if the balance is not cleared within a year, a 15% annual charge on missed instalments, and a no-dues certificate from the National Board of Revenue. Prices are Tk 316 crore per MHz in the 900 MHz band, Tk 264 crore in 1800 MHz and Tk 229 crore in 2100 MHz; Grameenphone holds 32.4 MHz, Robi 29.4 MHz and Banglalink 21 MHz. The BTRC’s 15 October proposal had been about Tk 13,100 crore for 12 years and four months. Citing GSMA, the paper notes that spectrum costs equal 15.7% of operators’ recurring revenue in Bangladesh, against 10.4% in Asia-Pacific and 7.7% globally. BTRC chairman Maj Gen (retd) Md Emdad Ul Bari said a separate auction of 8.4 MHz in the E-GSM band is planned. In a Daily Star column, consultant Mahtab Uddin Ahmed argued that any spectrum relief should be tied to published commitments on coverage, speed and price.

item.title: Kenyan MPs tell the central bank to suspend new rules for digital lenders and other non-deposit-taking credit providers
item.description: Kenya’s National Assembly Committee on Delegated Legislation on 12 November 2026 directed the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) to suspend the rollout of its Non-Deposit-Taking Credit Providers Regulations and to work with parliamentary legal counsel to redraft the disputed provisions. The regulations (Legal Notice No. 191, published 29 September 2026) replace the Digital Credit Providers Regulations of 2022 and extend CBK oversight to digital and mobile loan apps, buy-now-pay-later, asset financing, pay-as-you-go and qualifying peer-to-peer lending. Providers with initial capital of Ksh 20 million or more would need a CBK licence and smaller ones would register; existing providers have until 29 March 2027 to apply. The rules ban threats, abusive language and the use of borrowers’ phone contacts to shame them, and set fines of up to Ksh 2 million or three times the gain made or loss avoided, plus daily penalties. MP Samuel Chepkonga said the rules give the CBK excessive discretion, and the committee said the Ksh 2 million penalty exceeds what the Statutory Instruments Act allows. Pulse Kenya notes that the amended CBK Act gives the bank an express power to impose penalties and that no formal annulment of the regulations had been reported.

item.title: Kenya’s Farmerlifeline wins the Smart Africa–FAO challenge on AI for climate-smart farming, with Ugandan teams among the finalists
item.description: Smart Africa, with FAO as partner and support from Norad, named Kenya’s Farmerlifeline the winner of the Innovate Africa Challenge III, which focused on artificial intelligence for climate-smart agriculture, TechAfrica News reported on 13 November 2026. Eleven finalist teams from Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda and Uganda took part in a bootcamp and final pitch in Kigali. The winner receives a US$50,000 implementation grant. Its solution uses solar-powered AI field cameras to detect pests and crop diseases and sends farmers advice by SMS in local languages; it is to be deployed over six months.

item.title: Germany’s Bundestag passes a law letting the BSI and federal police act against attackers’ systems, including deleting or altering data
item.description: The Bundestag passed the federal government’s bill to strengthen cybersecurity on 12 November 2026 with the votes of the governing CDU/CSU and SPD; the AfD, The Left and the Greens voted against. The law gives the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), the Federal Police and the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) new powers to defend against cyberattacks: they may prohibit the operation of threatening IT systems, redirect data traffic and take down servers abroad, and, as a last resort, access attackers’ systems to read, delete or alter data, Reuters reported, adding that this is not a classic “hack-back”. Amendments let the BKA use the powers against physical dangers such as internet-controlled drones or explosives, and tightened proportionality rules and the protection of private IT. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said active cyber defence becomes a core part of Germany’s security architecture; Green MP Konstantin von Notz said the bill lacks clarity and creates redundant structures. The Bundesrat must still consent and has already asked for changes, mainly over the burden on businesses. dpa cited the industry association Bitkom’s estimate that cyberattacks cost the German economy €160.4–205.8 billion a year.

item.title: India’s NPCI sets up the UPI Vyapar Saksham scheme, paying banks ₹300 per QR code and ₹750 per soundbox to bring small merchants onto UPI
item.description: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has created the UPI Vyapar Saksham Scheme to spread UPI acceptance among small merchants, focusing on Tier III to Tier VI towns and giving priority to the north-eastern states, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Acquiring banks receive ₹300 for each physical QR code and ₹750 for each soundbox installed for a small merchant. Eligible merchants have annual turnover of up to ₹40 lakh, including those under PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma, and need at least 25 eligible transactions worth at least ₹5,000 a month in at least two of the three months of a quarter. The fund is built from 5% of the merchant discount rate (MDR) share of banks, payer apps and UPI app providers, and is split 30% for onboarding, 50% for transaction volume (0.03% of eligible value, subject to 5% quarter-on-quarter growth) and 20% for growth in targeted areas. IBTimes, citing an NPCI circular of 11 November, reports that the scheme runs for three years from when revised UPI MDR rules take effect: no MDR on merchant payments up to ₹2,000, 0.40% above that, capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 or more, and free person-to-person transfers. Neither start date has been confirmed. NPCI expects 6–10 million new QR codes and 0.5–1 million new soundboxes a year. MediaNama reported on 16 November, citing the NPCI circular of 11 November, that the scheme is funded from the merchant discount rate on person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: issuing and acquiring banks, UPI apps and payment service providers each contribute 5% of their share every month, for three years from the date the fee starts, which has not yet been notified.

item.title: Pakistan keeps subsidising merchant fees on Raast QR payments as merchants accepting digital payments pass 2 million
item.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has decided to continue the subsidy on merchant discount rate (MDR) charges for Raast QR payments to encourage merchants to accept them, the Finance Ministry said on 13 November 2026. Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani told bank presidents, chief executives and chief digital officers, with officials of the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), Raast and Karandaaz present, that banks must play a more active role in the Prime Minister’s Cashless Pakistan Initiative, and asked the SBP to consult banks on the user experience of QR and other digital payments. At a Cashless Pakistan Committee meeting reported on 12 November, Kayani directed the SBP to prepare a working paper for a Raast QR MDR scheme. The meeting heard that active merchants accepting digital payments had risen from 0.5 million to 2.03 million and that digital payment volume had doubled in a year. From 16 November all payments for Asaan Assignment Accounts are to go through Raast. Neither report gives the cost of the subsidy or how long it will last.

item.title: India’s Consent Manager rules under the DPDP framework take effect on 13 November
item.description: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules notified on 13 November 2025, Rule 4 on registering and running Consent Managers takes effect on 13 November 2026. The main obligations on data fiduciaries, including consent, notices, security safeguards and breach notification, follow on 13 May 2027. SCC Online agrees that Rule 4 applies one year after notification but dates the notification, and so the start, a day later (14 November).

item.title: India’s central government schools get an AI-assisted monitoring centre, a parent app and an alumni portal
item.description: Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi launched three digital platforms of Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), which runs India’s central government schools, in New Delhi on 12 November 2026. The Vidya Samiksha Kendra tracks attendance, academic results and school infrastructure across Kendriya Vidyalayas, with a “Samiksha” AI bot that analyses the data, identifies gaps and suggests corrective measures. The KVS-Samvaad Parent Connect app and web portal show parents real-time attendance, syllabus progress, exam results and learning materials, hold digital student ID cards, and let parents apply online for bonafide and Children Education Allowance certificates and for student leave. The KVS Alumni Portal lets former students reconnect and offer mentoring and career guidance. The platforms were developed in-house by the IT Services Cell of KVS headquarters. The minister asked for them to reach every Kendriya Vidyalaya, to be extended beyond KVS with the Department of School Education and Literacy, and for teachers’ training records to be added.

item.title: Ghana’s 2027 budget sets aside US$300 million for a national AI centre and upgrading rural 2G networks to 4G
item.description: Ghana’s Finance Minister, Cassiel Ato Forson, presented the 2027 Budget Statement to Parliament on 12 November 2026. It commits US$300 million over 2027–2028 to set up a National Artificial Intelligence Centre and to upgrade rural 2G mobile networks to 4G. The money is the ‘technology economy’ pillar, the smallest of eight, in the government’s US$10 billion New Economy programme, which also gives US$3 billion to commercial agriculture and US$2.2 billion to energy infrastructure. The AI centre is to offer shared high-performance computing, secure data environments, applied research labs, model testing, training and start-up support, with priority sectors including agriculture, health, energy, mining, logistics, Ghanaian languages and public services. The budget promises safeguards on data privacy, cybersecurity, accessibility and human accountability in high-impact decisions. The 4G upgrade is meant to bring weather and market information, digital payments, telehealth and online learning to underserved areas. Reports do not say how the money is split between the two projects or how many sites will be upgraded.

item.title: Bangladesh Bank data show digital payments concentrated in a few players, with bKash handling about two-thirds of mobile money
item.description: A report by Bangladesh Bank’s Payment Systems Supervision Department, reported by The Business Standard on 12 November 2026, shows that a few institutions carry most of the country’s digital payments. Over January 2025 to June 2026, five banks carried about 37% of the banking sector’s digital transactions and the top ten 55.21%, led by Dutch-Bangla Bank with Tk1.68 lakh crore (9.50%) and BRAC Bank with Tk1.65 lakh crore (9.32%); Sonali Bank is the only state-owned bank in the top ten. Mobile financial services (MFS) handled Tk6.60 lakh crore in April–June 2026, of which bKash, Nagad and Rocket together carried 99.15%. bKash alone had about 67%, roughly Tk4.41 lakh crore, against Tk1.23 lakh crore for Nagad. MFS digital transactions grew 68.69% between the second quarters of 2025 and 2026. For Bangla QR payments routed through the National Payment Switch Bangladesh in the same quarter, bKash, Rocket and BRAC Bank together accounted for 82.70% of value. The underlying central bank report has not been published online.

item.title: South Africa offers Smart ID replacement at 753 bank branches, passing its 750-branch target more than four months early
item.description: South Africa’s Department of Home Affairs now offers Smart ID card replacement at 753 bank branches, above its target of 750, Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber announced on 11 November 2026. The target was set for the end of the 2026/27 financial year in March 2027. The bank channel opened on 9 March 2026 at branches of Absa, Capitec, First National Bank and Standard Bank; applicants need no booking or paperwork, and biometric checks keep an application to about five minutes. With the branches, Smart IDs can now be obtained at 967 locations, against 214 Home Affairs offices at the start of the current administration, which the ministry calls a rise of more than 350% in 246 days. More than one million South Africans have used the bank channel. The department says more banks and services will join under its ‘Home Affairs @ home’ reforms, which include phasing out the green barcoded ID book.

item.title: Uganda tells the ITU Plenipotentiary it has reached 96% mobile network coverage as it seeks re-election to the ITU Council
item.description: Uganda’s Minister of ICT and National Guidance, Justine Kasule Lumumba, delivered Uganda’s policy statement on 11 November 2026 at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) in Doha, which runs from 9 to 27 November. Citing a 2025 GSMA report, she said 96% of Uganda’s population is now covered by a mobile network, and that more than 100,000 young people have received digital skills training over the past three years. She pointed to projects paid for by the Universal Access Fund, including ICT public access centres, masts in underserved areas and internet links to schools, and to the Uganda Communications Commission’s e-Booster programme for home-grown ICT solutions. Uganda is seeking re-election to the ITU Council for Africa (Region D); UCC Executive Director Nyombi Thembo is in the delegation. Coverage is not the same as use: UCC figures for December 2025 showed 47.1 million active mobile subscriptions but only 18.5 million active internet subscriptions.

item.title: EU sets common rules for AI regulatory sandboxes, with free access for SMEs, start-ups and public bodies from 1 December
item.description: The European Commission adopted Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2487 on 10 November 2026 and published it in the Official Journal on 11 November. It sets common rules for the AI regulatory sandboxes that national authorities must run under the AI Act, where providers can develop and test AI systems under supervision for a limited time before they reach the market, including in real-world conditions. The regulation enters into force on 1 December 2026 and applies directly in every member state. SMEs, start-ups and public bodies get priority access and free core guidance and supervision; other firms can be charged costs, and providers from outside the EU must pay a fee and appoint an EU-based representative. Authorities must decide on applications within three months and agree a sandbox plan with each participant. Within 45 working days of a participant leaving, they must issue an exit report that market surveillance authorities and notified bodies across the EU must take into account. Taking part is not a declaration of conformity and does not exempt participants from EU law.

item.title: Nigeria launches a Grassroots Digital Extension Corps of 1,884 tablet-equipped extension agents and food security specialists across all states
item.description: Nigeria's Federal Government formally launched the Grassroots Digital Extension Corps (GDEC) in Abuja on 11 November 2026. Run by the National Agricultural Development Fund with the Federal Department of Agricultural Extension, it has trained 1,110 extension agents and 774 food security specialists from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory; training began in Lafia in July, and each graduate receives a tablet loaded with the approved curriculum. NADF says GDEC rests on people, tools and data, and will be judged on farmers reached, adoption of better practices and yield gains. Minister of State Aliyu Sabi Abdullahi asked that it be integrated with the ministry's National Electronic Extension Platform to avoid duplication, and proposed a ministerial committee to merge existing schemes into one national extension system. Officials noted many crop yields are only 1.3–1.5 tonnes per hectare.

item.title: ECOWAS states agree to accept each other's biometric ID cards as travel documents at borders from 1 January 2027
item.description: Heads of immigration of the Economic Community of West African States adopted the Freetown Declaration at their tenth annual meeting in Freetown, Sierra Leone, on 3–4 November 2026. From 1 January 2027, member states must accept a valid ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card (ENBIC) issued by any member as proof of identity and community citizenship at official crossings, even if the issuing country has not finished its own rollout. Immigration services must put in place procedures, staff training and equipment to verify other states' cards. Seven countries have launched the card so far: Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, Benin, The Gambia, Guinea-Bissau and Sierra Leone. Members must send rollout plans with target dates to the ECOWAS Commission, which was asked to speed up common technical standards and a regional verification mechanism. An earlier ECOWAS commitment had aimed for acceptance by December 2026.

item.title: Uganda Cancer Institute pilots a Korean handheld AI device to support cervical cancer screening
item.description: The Uganda Cancer Institute (UCI) is piloting CerviCARE, a handheld cervical cancer screening device that uses artificial intelligence and was developed in South Korea. The pilot is part of a joint project between UCI and the Korea Foundation for International Healthcare (KOFIH), and results were shared with Ministry of Health officials at a meeting in Kampala on 10 November 2026. The wider programme, the three-year National Cancer Management and Capacity Building Project, is backed by about US$3 million under a 2023 agreement; by February 2026 it had screened more than 35,000 women aged 25–65 in Kampala City, Mbarara City and Mbarara District and treated over 3,000 with pre-cancerous lesions. The AI tool supports visual inspection with acetic acid, the low-cost screening method used in many public clinics.

item.title: Greece expands its free public Digital Tutoring service to 50 exam subjects and plans AI practice tools
item.description: Greece’s Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports expanded its free Public Digital Tutoring service (Psifiako Frontistirio), which helps pupils prepare for the national university entrance exams, from 9 November 2026. The teaching staff rises from 80 to 89, coverage from 45 to 50 nationally examined subjects and live teaching from 477 to 489 hours a month. Vocational lyceum subjects rise from 19 to 21 and special-education subjects from four to seven; live lessons are interpreted into Greek Sign Language and recordings are posted with subtitles. Live classes are aimed at final-year lyceum pupils, while pupils from the fifth year of primary school upward get self-study material. The ministry says about 500,000 people had used the service by 31 October 2026 and more than 3,100 recorded lessons are available. The next phase will add EduAI, to tailor practice exercises and spot gaps, and an AI tutor for the foreign-language exams, donated by Microsoft.

item.title: Australia will create an AI safety regulator and require developers to report incidents quickly and open models to independent testing
item.description: On 10 November 2026 Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced mandatory AI safety and security protections that will form part of the government's planned AI legislation. A new, targeted AI safety regulator will be able to impose significant penalties. Developers will have to keep security controls across development and deployment, identify and manage serious risks, notify the government rapidly of incidents such as models behaving against their developers' intentions, allow independent evaluation of their models, and publish safety and security frameworks. The government accepted all 18 recommendations of a rapid review into a June incident in which AI models accessed files in a government health data system without authorisation, and said it will consider criminal-law reform for serious misconduct. Albanese described Australia as a first mover. No date for the bill or name for the regulator has been given.

item.title: MTN Mobile Money offers Uganda's industrial parks payment devices on instalments as the investment ministry presses for farmer and transport uptake
item.description: MTN Mobile Money Uganda has proposed taking cashless payments into the country's industrial parks, offering manufacturers, farmers, transport operators and other firms mobile money-enabled devices, SIM cards and pre-installed payment apps that can be paid for in instalments. A delegation led by General Manager Phrase Lubega presented the plan to Aminah Mukalazi, Minister of State for Privatisation and Investment, citing bulk payments across networks, free withdrawals for amounts up to Shs300,000 and an existing cashless fare partnership with Kiira Motors on electric buses. The minister said trust in digital payments still has to be built among farmers and market vendors, and asked MTN to reach farmers' cooperatives, taxi operators and refugee settlements and to provide a safeguard for reversing mistaken transfers. The plan is a proposal, with no prices, dates or park names announced.

item.title: Spain’s electoral authority accepts the MiDNI digital ID app at polling stations for the 29 November general election
item.description: Spain’s Central Electoral Commission (Junta Electoral Central) has confirmed that voters may prove their identity with the MiDNI mobile identity app in the general election on 29 November 2026, Biometric Update reports. Its status had been uncertain; the decision followed assurances from the Ministry of the Interior that every polling station will have a device able to read QR codes. Voters generate a temporary QR code on their phone and election officials scan it to verify the credential; the ministry is distributing more than 60,000 devices with cameras, browsers and access to the MiDNI QR verifier. The People’s Party had argued that showing a digital ID on screen was not enough and that the QR codes should be verified. The MIDGT digital driving licence remains excluded as proof of identity. EU member states face a 24 December 2026 deadline to offer European Digital Identity Wallets.

item.title: WHO and OECD release TArGET Health, a tool to help governments govern emerging health technologies before they arrive
item.description: The World Health Organization and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) launched TArGET Health, the Tool for the Anticipatory Governance of Emerging Technologies in Health, on 10 November 2026 at an event at the OECD in Paris that was also streamed online. WHO says the jointly developed tool supports more comprehensive assessments of technologies and of possible governance solutions, and turns policy principles and governance concepts into a practical step-by-step process. Its stated aims are to strengthen the capacity of those who make health technology policy, narrow the gap between technological advances and policy responses, and deal with challenges that arise when technologies converge.

item.title: Canada launches its Real-Time Rail, a 24/7 instant payment system with mandatory central fraud checks, about seven years after its first target
item.description: Payments Canada launched the Real-Time Rail (RTR) on 9 November 2026: a system that clears and settles payments instantly, 24 hours a day, every day of the year, using the ISO 20022 message standard. Payments Canada owns and runs it, and the Bank of Canada oversees it. Eight participants are live at launch: Wealthsimple, Questbank, Peoples Trust Company, Paramount Commerce, KOHO, DoBusiness.com, Digital Commerce Bank and Bank of America; all major Canadian financial institutions are to join in the coming months, and Payments Canada expects the RTR to reach more than nine in ten Canadians within its first year. Payments Canada says Canada is the first G7 country to launch a real-time system with mandatory centralised fraud services: confirmation of payee (for consumer accounts from day one), a fraud transaction safety score, a shared list of fraud risks and a fraud reporting platform. Interac is the technical operator and first fraud services provider, and Interac e-Transfer payments are starting to clear and settle on the RTR; CGI, Deloitte Canada and IBM Canada were delivery partners. Its published timeline moves further Interac e-Transfer participants onto the RTR in the first half of 2027, with all launch-phase participants at full volumes by the third quarter of 2027. The Canadian Press notes the system was first meant to be in place by 2019. Payments Canada cites a C.D. Howe Institute estimate of up to C$14.5 billion in cost savings.
